title: New Blood by Morand wins at Paul Ricard as Murphy is penalised
dek: Christian Klien, Gary Hirsch and Pierre Ragues won the 4 Hours of Le Castellet by 5.518s in the New Blood by Morand Morgan-Judd, after a late Murphy penalty ended Berthon's chase of the Signatech Alpine.

chapters.title: A title race with two rounds to run
text: The 4 Hours of Le Castellet on 14 September 2014 was the penultimate round of the European Le Mans Series, and the LMP2 championship was tight. Signatech Alpine, the reigning champions, arrived four points clear after winning at the Red Bull Ring, with Paul-Loup Chatin, Nelson Panciatici and Oliver Webb having grown into a formidable unit after a poor start at Silverstone. Race Performance was a further 11 points back. Three rounds had produced three different winners, and the paddock was returning from a long summer break at a circuit where the Ligier of Thiriet by TDS was expected to enjoy an aerodynamic edge on the Mistral Straight.

The entry list carried several fresh faces. Murphy Prototypes was back after missing the Red Bull Ring and drafted in the Brazilian Pipo Derani, who had tested for the team at Snetterton, to join Nathanael Berthon and Rodolfo Gonzalez in the Oreca. Sébastien Loeb Racing returned with a revised line-up, Vincent Capillaire sharing the Oreca with the single-seater racers Arthur Pic and Andrea Roda, both new to prototypes. Greaves Motorsport gave Johnny Mowlem a seat alongside the 16-year-old Matthew McMurry. Jota Sport, buoyed by its Le Mans success in June, wanted a fourth straight pole to go with its championship push. BoP changes before the weekend were confined to the GT cars.

Free practice offered no clear favourite. Panciatici put the Signatech Alpine on top on Saturday morning with a 1:50.117, 0.203s clear of Thiriet by TDS. In the afternoon Christian Klien took the New Blood by Morand Morgan-Judd to the head of the order on 1:49.473, a mere 0.004s ahead of Jota's Zytek, with the Thiriet Ligier third and the Alpine fourth.

chapters.title: Berthon ends Jota's pole run
text: Berthon took pole in the 20-minute session on Sunday morning, his 1:47.837 in the Murphy Prototypes Oreca-Nissan beating Jota's Zytek-Nissan by 0.289s and ending the Jota team's perfect record on the front of the grid this season. It was 0.566s quicker than last year's pole time and gave Murphy its first pole since Hungaroring 2013. Berthon said the team had worked hard to perfect the car in free practice, adding that the race was a long one. Derani was nominated to start the race from pole.

Harry Tincknell's 1:48.126 put the #38 Jota car on the front row, with Klien third for New Blood by Morand on 1:48.420. Franck Mailleux placed the Race Performance Oreca-Judd fourth, 0.757s off pole. The championship leaders were only fifth: Signatech Alpine's 1:48.956 beat the Sébastien Loeb Racing Oreca of Pic by just two thousandths of a second. Thiriet by TDS, Greaves and Pegasus followed in the order, while the second Greaves entry, with McMurry, was last of the LMP2 runners in qualifying on 1:51.502. Conditions were ideal and 37 cars lined up for a 13:00 start.

chapters.title: Derani holds off Tincknell, McMurry out at the first corner
text: Derani led from pole and, in his first LMP2 race, kept Tincknell's Jota Zytek behind for the opening half-hour. Trouble struck the field immediately: the #41 Greaves Zytek was crashed by McMurry at the first corner and was out on the opening lap, leaving the car not classified. Pegasus Racing's Morgan-Nissan also failed to reach the finish. The opening stint was otherwise played out among the Murphy, Jota, New Blood and Signatech cars.

chapters.title: Four cars in the lead fight
text: The order changed through the first round of pit stops. Pierre Ragues took over the lead for New Blood by Morand and Gary Hirsch then drove a long stint to build what became a winning gap. Hirsch took Simon Dolan's Jota car around the outside at Le Beausset and held off the charging Panciatici, pulling away from the Alpine. Gonzalez, who had to complete the silver driver's mandatory 140 minutes for Murphy, led during the pit-stop sequences and fought wheel to wheel with Klien on the Mistral Straight, the two cars running inches apart at around 175mph.

Jota split Dolan's stints, with Filipe Albuquerque driving the penultimate hour, but the team lacked straight-line speed and was unable to run with the leaders. The Greaves Zytek of Luciano Bacheta and Mark Shulzhitskiy ran as high as third at stages, while the Thiriet by TDS Ligier was out of the race after 89 laps. Klien went to the front with just over an hour remaining, passing Gonzalez.

chapters.title: Klien wins, Murphy penalised in the closing stint
text: With 45 minutes to go the order was Klien first and Chatin second, with Berthon, who had taken over the Murphy Oreca for the last stint, closing in. Chatin and Berthon ran nose to tail at one point, separated by a thousandth of a second on one lap, and a fight for second place, or even the win, loomed. Then Murphy was handed a penalty for refuelling at its final stop with the engine running. It cost Berthon time, and he was also baulked on entering the pit lane. His chance of challenging the leaders was gone.

Klien, who double-stinted a set of hard Dunlops, controlled the gap to Chatin in the final half-hour and crossed the line 5.518s ahead after 4:00:33.427 and 125 laps. Murphy still held onto third, ahead of the Jota Zytek of Dolan, Tincknell and Albuquerque, which took fourth when the Greaves Zytek of Bacheta and Shulzhitskiy lost the place on the final lap. The top five all finished on the lead lap. Sébastien Loeb Racing and Race Performance were the only other classified LMP2 cars, two and three laps down.

chapters.title: New Blood win, Signatech extend the lead
text: It was the first ELMS victory of the season for New Blood by Morand Racing. Klien said the team had deserved the win and he had managed the tyres in the closing laps. Hirsch said it was a year to the day since he first met team boss Benoit Morand, and that he hoped to repeat the win at Estoril. Morand confirmed that Klien was under contract for 2015 and that the team intended to stay with the Morgan-Judd package, while evaluating a second car.

Murphy Prototypes left with pole and a podium, but with regrets. Berthon said he believed the team could have won and admitted to disappointment, although he felt pole and a podium were something to be proud of. For Signatech Alpine, second place was enough to extend the championship lead to 10 points with 26 available at the final round at Estoril. Team principal Philippe Sinault said the aggressive strategy had been designed to take points from the main rivals, and that the team was targeting a possible step up to the FIA World Endurance Championship in 2015.

Jota Sport's fourth place kept it in the hunt, though it now trailed by 10 points and, even with a win at Estoril, would need another car to finish between it and Signatech. Race Performance salvaged six points for seventh. Four rounds had produced four different winning teams, with Morgan taking two, Zytek one and Alpine one.
The next stop is the 4 Hours of Estoril on 19 October, the final round of the 2014 season.

facts.v: Nathanael Berthon took pole with 1:47.837 in the Murphy Oreca-Nissan, the first pole for a car other than Jota's this season.
